summary: Isengard refuses the Winter Crown: forts on the march, gifts to the steadings, and an answer to Fandanar that is either never to kneel or a seat at the Accord.

refusal_of_850.name: The Refusal of 850
refusal_of_850.desc: When the kings of Coldor united the frozen interior, the hall of Isengard said no, and has said it at every midwinter since. The refusal is a pride, a burden and a wall.

warlords_hall.name: The Warlord's Hall
warlords_hall.desc: A black iron bench, a long table and a dozen chiefs who will each speak first. The warlord rules by being the loudest voice that nobody dares to answer.

iron_crown.name: The Iron Crown of Isengard
iron_crown.desc: No one wears it, and every fort swears by it. The hall has learned to rule without a crown by making each fort answerable to the bench.

march_watch.name: Watch on the March
march_watch.desc: A beacon on every tower and a rider in every pass. Not a patrol crosses the ridge unseen.

forts_hold.name: The Forts Hold
forts_hold.desc: The horns have sounded and the walls are manned. Every stone of the march has been counted, and every stone answers.

never_kneel_oath.name: Never Kneel
never_kneel_oath.desc: The warlord has sworn on the black bench that Isengard bends to no crown. The oath steadies the hall and costs it friends.

heavy_hosts_drilled.name: The Heavy Hosts
heavy_hosts_drilled.desc: Shield-walls drilled until the rows move as one wall of iron and linden. Isengard's hosts are slow to start and slower to break.

the_north_held.name: The North Held
the_north_held.desc: When the south burned, the hall kept its forts and its fields, and the north did not break. Winter itself was on Isengard's side.

marriage_offer.title: A Daughter of the Iron Hall
marriage_offer.desc: Envoys of Isengard stand in the great hall of Fandanar with a gift of black iron and a request in the warlord's own words. He offers one of his daughters to the Winter Crown's house, so that two halls that have glared across a border for three centuries might share a hearth.

iron_halls_promise.title: The Iron Hall Stands Behind Us
iron_halls_promise.desc: A rider in black mail reaches the steading at dusk with the warlord's word: no crown will take this hearth while Isengard holds iron. He swears it on the steading's own fire, before witnesses, and leaves before the meal is poured.

focuses.name: The Iron Hall
focuses.desc: Ezhan Isenmar sits where the warlords of Isengard have always sat, on a bench of black iron older than the border forts. Every chief who brings a gift to the hall leaves with a seat and a debt.

focuses.name: The Warband Chiefs
focuses.desc: The chiefs of the warbands boast of the refusal at every feast, and the warlord lets them. A boast heard in the hall is a boast that will be paid for in the field.

focuses.name: The Old Refusal
focuses.desc: The kings of Coldor offered Isengard a crown to share and a seat to kneel in, and the hall said no. The word is carved above its door, and every new chief touches it before he speaks.

effects.tooltip: In 850 the hall said no. It still says no.

focuses.name: Counsel of the Forges
focuses.desc: The smiths of the iron hills sit nearest the warlord's bench, for they make the blades that give the hall its voice. Their counsel is short: more iron, more forts, less talk of kings.

focuses.name: Law of the Hall
focuses.desc: The old customs are cut into the hall's pillars and read aloud at midwinter, so that no chief may say he did not know them. Fewer quarrels now end with a drawn blade.

focuses.name: Heirs of Isenmar
focuses.desc: The warlord's sons and nephews are sent to the border forts at twelve winters. They come back hard, loyal, and deaf to the word crown.

focuses.name: One Hall, Many Forts
focuses.desc: Every fort on the march now swears to the hall by name, and the hall answers for every fort. A warlord's bench has grown into something near a crown, though nobody in Isengard will say so aloud.

focuses.name: Man the March
focuses.desc: Coldor's border runs along old ridges and drovers' tracks, and the forts that watch it have been manned every winter since 850. The warlord orders them filled before the snow and stocked for a siege longer than anyone expects.

focuses.name: Count the Stones
focuses.desc: Masons walk the walls with knotted cords and chalk what each tower needs on its doorframe. What the forts lack is quarried before the thaw.

focuses.name: Watchtowers of the March
focuses.desc: A beacon is laid on every tower, each within sight of the next. No patrol of Coldor crosses the ridge without a hundred eyes noting its banners.

focuses.name: The Ninth Fort
focuses.desc: At the narrowest of the passes stands the Ninth Fort, where Brana has held the gate for eleven winters. She asks the hall for walls and gets them; she asks for nothing else.

focuses.name: Meet Them at the Forts
focuses.desc: The horns blow along the whole ridge and every fort answers. Isengard fights where it is strongest: behind stone, with the hall's iron at its back.

focuses.name: Stone upon Stone
focuses.desc: More masons are sent to the forts, and the hall itself is walled. An Isengard that has been wounded once means not to be wounded twice.

focuses.name: Ride to the Forts
focuses.desc: Riders carry the warlord's word to every fort: the border will not wait on Coldor's pleasure. If a quarrel must be fought, Isengard will choose the ground.

focuses.name: The March Remembers
focuses.desc: When the horns fall silent, the dead of the border are named at the hall's door, fort by fort. Whatever the forts cost, the hall still stands.

effects.tooltip: Whatever the forts cost, the hall still stands.

focuses.name: Winter Gifts
focuses.desc: The long winters hurt the steadings along the march worst of all. The warlord sends sledges of salt and barley before the passes close, and asks only that the gift be remembered.

focuses.name: The Gift-Giver
focuses.desc: Veska has carried the warlord's gifts for twenty winters and knows every chief by his mother's name. She turns a sack of barley into a debt of honour without once naming it.

focuses.name: Salt and Iron for the Clans
focuses.desc: Salt cures the winter meat and iron tips the winter spear. Isengard has plenty of the second and trades for the first, and the clans learn which hall sells fair.

focuses.name: Granaries of the Hall
focuses.desc: Stone granaries rise beside the forts, filled each autumn from the hall's own fields. When the hard winters come, no steading that kept faith with Isengard goes hungry.

focuses.name: Hosts at the Winter Moot
focuses.desc: At the Winter Moot the warlord's table is longer than Fandanar's and the ale is better. Chiefs who have eaten at it do not forget whose roof was warm.

focuses.name: Oath-Brothers of the March
focuses.desc: The warlord's envoys offer the border clans what no crown gives: a spear at their gate, sworn on iron before witnesses. Clans that are weary of paying Fandanar's price listen closely.

focuses.name: The Iron Hall's Bread
focuses.desc: Loaves from the hall's ovens are carried to the farthest steadings, and where they go, men speak of the warlord kindly. It is a small gift, and it wins more than a fort.

focuses.name: The Envoys from Fandanar
focuses.desc: Fandanar sends cloaked envoys with soft words and sealed scrolls. They speak of the Accord, of safety in numbers, of a seat at a table of equals.

focuses.name: Never Kneel
focuses.desc: The warlord receives the envoys standing and answers them standing. Isengard bends to iron, he says, and to nothing that was not forged in its own hills.

focuses.name: A Seat at Fandanar
focuses.desc: Not every voice in the hall is for refusal. Some chiefs would trade a little pride for a seat at the Accord's table and a border that costs them fewer winters of watching.

focuses.name: The Free North
focuses.desc: Isengard's envoys carry a different word to the northern clans: that the Winter Crown is no crown of theirs, and that the north has room for more than one hall.

focuses.name: A Daughter of the Hall
focuses.desc: A marriage may cost less than a war. The warlord offers one of his daughters to the house of Fandanar, and Fandanar must weigh whether to take iron into its blood.

focuses.name: Iron Against the Crown
focuses.desc: When the forts have been proved and the wider world stands near the edge of a larger war, the hall may stop answering and begin asking. Isengard's chiefs name the lands on the march that they mean to take back.

focuses.name: Under the Accord's Banner
focuses.desc: Isengard has sworn to the Accord, and the warlord stands beneath a banner he once spat upon. His chiefs grumble, but they are the better fed for it.

focuses.name: The Hall Unbowed
focuses.desc: Whatever comes, the hall stands, and its door still bears the word its founders cut in it. The chiefs renew their oaths on the black bench, and the oaths are heavier than before.

focuses.name: Kin Across the March
focuses.desc: Families split by the old border visit one another again, and trade crosses it without a toll. The cold between the two halls thaws a little, though it does not vanish.

focuses.name: The Iron Hills
focuses.desc: Isengard sits on iron, and iron is its argument in every council. The warlord sends new gangs into the hills with orders to dig for the hall.

focuses.name: Deep Shafts
focuses.desc: Where the old drifts ran dry, new shafts go down past the water line on timber props. The miners sing as they climb, to keep count of the ones below.

focuses.name: Forge-Halls
focuses.desc: Long halls with a dozen hearths apiece are raised beside the pits, so that ore need never travel far to meet a hammer. The ring of the anvils carries to the border.

focuses.name: Sledge-Ways
focuses.desc: Plank roads, iced each night, carry the hall's iron from the hills to the forts on broad sledges. What took a month by pack-beast now takes a week.

focuses.name: Iron for the Forts
focuses.desc: Every fort has its own forge now, and every forge its quota of blades and spear-heads. When the horns sound, the garrisons will not wait on a cart from the hall.

focuses.name: The Iron Host
focuses.desc: The hall's spearmen drill in the fort yards from thaw to first frost, under chiefs who have fought the same ridges for a lifetime. They know the march better than they know their own hearths.

focuses.name: Shield-Wall Drill
focuses.desc: Linden shields rimmed with iron lock edge to edge, and the ranks learn to take a charge on the boss and answer with the spear. The drill-masters count the steps aloud until the men no longer need counting.

focuses.name: Valley Spears
focuses.desc: Long ash spears with leaf-blades come from the valley smithies in their thousands. A man with a spear and a shield behind him is worth three without.

focuses.name: Heavy Hosts
focuses.desc: The drums beat the slow pace of the march, and the whole host steps to it. An Isengard host does not hurry, and it does not stop.

focuses.name: Levy of the Valleys
focuses.desc: Each valley sends one man in five when the hall calls, with his bread and his blade. The roll is read in the fort yards, and none is struck from it but the dead.

focuses.name: Beyond the March
focuses.desc: News comes up the passes of a war far to the south, in lands the warlord has never seen. The hall must decide whether the world beyond the march is its business.

focuses.name: Hold the North
focuses.desc: The south may burn; the north will be held. The warlord calls every fort to full strength and tells his chiefs that a hall which keeps its own is no small thing in a dark year.

focuses.name: Iron for the Living
focuses.desc: A few of the warband chiefs say that Isengard's iron was never meant to rust behind a wall. If the living of the south are to stand against the dark, they will need blades, and Isengard has blades.

focuses.name: The Iron Companies March South
focuses.desc: The iron companies leave the forts in the first snow and take the long road south. Behind them the beacons burn on, tended by the old and the very young.

marriage.name: The Hall and the Crown Wed
